blocks.text: 拓展开放智能的边界
Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 Kimi K3 的后训练版本，后训练算力大幅增加。为实现跨数百个下游领域的大规模联合强化学习，我们优化了技术栈的每一层——强化学习框架、长上下文推理、训练效率、沙箱基础设施、rollout 调度，以及用于环境质量检查的共享平台——使每一份强化学习算力的投入都能带来稳定、可预期的回报。因此，K3.1 Pro 在每个领域都取得了持续提升。

blocks.text: K3.1 Pro 的长程编码能力也通过大规模强化学习得到增强。在一项内部测试中，它在 human-atlas 之上构建了一个集成训练与评估流水线的人体行走动力学模拟器；human-atlas 是一个开源的人体解剖模型，包含 296 个骨骼组件（含软骨）和 402 个肌肉组件。在 167 项任务和 420 次独立评审中，它分析实验结果、诊断问题并迭代改进行走控制器，使模拟人从数秒内瘫倒变为以交替步态连续行走 11.2 秒。当奖励塑形未能改善手臂运动时，K3.1 Pro 并未一味继续调整奖励：它对模拟器的动力学进行了开环探测，识别并纠正了肩部肌肉力臂计算中的 36 处错误，然后重新训练了控制器。

blocks.text: 网络安全
随着 K3.1 Pro 能力增强，我们相应投入了更大比例的努力来理解网络能力的来源，以及我们能在多大程度上控制它。因此，我们分析并评估了 K3.1 Pro 的漏洞研究能力，并在训练期间施加定向控制，以降低潜在滥用风险，同时保留通用实用性。

inlines.text: 随着 K3.1 Pro 能力增强，我们相应投入了更大比例的努力来理解网络能力的来源，以及我们能在多大程度上控制它。因此，我们分析并评估了 K3.1 Pro 的漏洞研究能力，并在训练期间施加定向控制，以降低潜在滥用风险，同时保留通用实用性。

blocks.text: 识别并移除网络相关数据。在开发过程中，我们观察到漏洞研究性能随着后训练规模扩大而稳步提升。追溯这一趋势的来源，我们发现网络相关内容嵌入在通用中期训练语料中，且网络相关任务存在于 RL 环境组合中——这是基于广泛数据训练的自然产物。在内部模型的初步实验中，我们发现若在中期训练或 RL 阶段均不移除数据，下游网络能力将大幅提升。这些发现为我们提供了具体的控制杠杆。对于 K3.1 Pro 的开放权重发布，我们在两个训练阶段均识别并移除了网络相关数据，同时保留了模型实用性所需的通用编程任务。我们将继续在每个训练阶段施加适当控制，网络相关数据的识别与限制便是其中一例。

blocks.text: 评估与结果。数据清洗后，我们在 xdev-bench-hard 上评估了 K3.1 Pro，这是我们内部的基准，由专家策划、基于源代码的漏洞发现与利用任务构成，经过校准以在当前能力水平上提供有意义的区分度。大多数任务忠实复现了 Linux 内核、Node.js、JavaScriptCore、Exim 和 VirGL 等软件中近期披露的漏洞，并启用了缓解措施。每个任务提供存在漏洞的源代码、简短的缺陷提示以及相应的二进制文件；智能体必须开发漏洞利用，在独立沙箱中实现任意代码执行，并获取一个秘密字符串以供自动验证。我们报告随机运行子集上的 pass@3，不设硬性超时或输出 token 限制。

blocks.text: 在 xdev-bench-hard 上，未采取这些风险降低措施（训练中期未移除网络相关数据，也未对网络相关 RL 环境进行过滤）的检查点，在 pass@3 下解决了 90.5% 的问题；最终的 K3.1 Pro 达到 81.0%。这一对比表明，相对于同一训练流程原本会产出的结果，数据移除显著降低了网络能力。与此同时，K3.1 Pro 较其前代有大幅提升，表明更强的通用编码与长程调试能力即使在定向数据移除之后，仍能泛化到网络任务上。K3.1 Pro 的网络能力仍落后于已公开可用至少三个月的前沿专有模型。我们将持续演进内部基准，使评估在模型能力不断进步时仍保持信息量。

inlines.text: 在 xdev-bench-hard 上，未采取这些风险降低措施（训练中期未移除网络相关数据，也未对网络相关 RL 环境进行过滤）的检查点，在 pass@3 下解决了 90.5% 的问题；最终的 K3.1 Pro 达到 81.0%。这一对比表明，相对于同一训练流程原本会产出的结果，数据移除显著降低了网络能力。与此同时，K3.1 Pro 较其前代有大幅提升，表明更强的通用编码与长程调试能力即使在定向数据移除之后，仍能泛化到网络任务上。K3.1 Pro 的网络能力仍落后于已公开可用至少三个月的前沿专有模型。我们将持续演进内部基准，使评估在模型能力不断进步时仍保持信息量。

blocks.text: 开放权重原则。这些评估构成了我们开放权重发布决策的框架。第一，我们力求不发布会拓展网络能力绝对前沿的开放权重。K3.1 Pro 的进攻性网络能力在设计上低于我们流程所能产出的水平，并且仍落后于前沿专有模型。第二，我们打算逐步提升开放权重中可用的网络能力。我们相信，以非歧视的方式提供 K3.1 Pro 有利于那些需要两用能力用于防御目的的人。当一个有能力的模型是开放的、并在用户自己控制的基础设施上运行时，更多团队获得了审计其维护代码的手段——包括很少接受专门安全审查的遗留系统。我们相信，让这种能力逐步扩散——而不是集中在少数专有系统中——最终会让所有软件更加安全。

blocks.text: Advancing the Frontier of Open Intelligence

inlines.text: Advancing the Frontier of Open Intelligence

blocks.text: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute. To enable large-scale joint RL across hundreds of downstream domains, we optimized every layer of the stack — the RL framework, long-context inference, training efficiency, sandbox infrastructure, rollout scheduling, and a shared platform for environment quality checks — so that each increment of RL compute delivers stable, predictable returns. As a result, K3.1 Pro achieves consistent gains in every domain.

blocks.text: Across coding, agentic, and knowledge benchmarks, K3.1 Pro matches or approaches the strongest proprietary models. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon, our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2%, above K3's 55.95%.

blocks.text: K3.1 Pro's long-horizon coding capabilities are also strengthened through large-scale reinforcement learning. In one internal test, it built a human walking dynamics simulator with integrated training and evaluation pipelines on top of human-atlas, an open-source anatomical model of the human body comprising 296 skeletal components, including cartilage, and 402 muscle components. Across 167 missions and 420 independent reviews, it analyzed experimental results, diagnosed problems, and iteratively refined the walking controller, enabling the simulated human to go from collapsing within seconds to walking continuously with alternating strides for 11.2 seconds. When reward shaping failed to improve arm motion, K3.1 Pro did not simply keep adjusting the reward: it ran open-loop probes of the simulator's dynamics, identified and corrected 36 errors in shoulder-muscle moment-arm calculations, and then retrained the controller.

blocks.text: 3D Modeling and Design

K3.1 Pro is strong at 3D creation and spatial reasoning. On BenchCAD, which tests 3D reconstruction from multi-view renderings through CAD code generation, K3.1 Pro scores 92.7% with tools, approaching the performance of Claude Opus 5.5 (96.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (95.9%). From a text brief, sketch, or reference image, it can infer shape, proportions, and spatial relationships to create usable 3D models. It also has a stronger grasp of existing asset libraries and model collections.

blocks.text: Finance

With stronger reasoning and agentic capability, K3.1 Pro is capable of end-to-end delivery of complete financial workflows. K3.1 Pro achieves state-of-the-art results on OfficeQA Pro v2 (64.4), which tests complex fiscal data analysis over real financial documents through retrieval, cross-document verification, and multi-step numerical reasoning. K3.1 Pro also improves over K3 on Frontier Finance, which measures support for complete investment workflows from screening to profitability analysis.

blocks.text: Financial analysis and investment research demand a high degree of factual accuracy. To address this, we made targeted improvements to K3.1 Pro's factual accuracy on real-world tasks and challenging prompts. On Kimi Hallu Bench Hard bench, an internal benchmark designed to stress-test factual accuracy, its claim-level hallucination rate fell from 23.4% for K3 to 8.3%, while the share of responses containing at least one factual error was just 42.4% of its predecessor's rate. (The evaluation is a stress test for factual accuracy, with examples deliberately crafted to probe situations where models are prone to errors. The reported rates do not represent overall error rates in daily use.)

blocks.text: Cybersecurity

As K3.1 Pro became more capable, we spent a correspondingly larger share of our effort understanding where cyber capability comes from, and how much of it we can control. We therefore analyzed and evaluated K3.1 Pro's vulnerability research capabilities, and applied targeted controls during training to reduce potential misuse risk while preserving general usefulness.

inlines.text: As K3.1 Pro became more capable, we spent a correspondingly larger share of our effort understanding where cyber capability comes from, and how much of it we can control. We therefore analyzed and evaluated K3.1 Pro's vulnerability research capabilities, and applied targeted controls during training to reduce potential misuse risk while preserving general usefulness.

blocks.text: Identifying and removing cyber-related data. During development, we observed vulnerability research performance improving steadily as post-training scaled. Tracing the source of this trend, we found that cyber-related content was embedded within the general mid-training corpus, and cyber-related tasks were present in the RL environment mix — a natural byproduct of training on broad data. In preliminary experiments on internal models, we found that without data removal at either the mid-training or the RL stage, downstream cyber capability would increase substantially. These findings gave us a concrete lever for control. For the open-weight release of K3.1 Pro, we identified and removed cyber-related data from both training stages, while retaining the general-purpose coding tasks needed for model usefulness. We will continue to apply appropriate controls at every training stage, of which cyber-related data identification and restriction is one example.

blocks.text: Evaluation and results. After data cleaning, we evaluated K3.1 Pro on xdev-bench-hard, our in-house benchmark of expert-curated, source-code-based vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks, calibrated to provide meaningful differentiation at our current capability level. Most tasks faithfully reproduce recently disclosed vulnerabilities in software such as the Linux kernel, Node.js, JavaScriptCore, Exim, and VirGL, with mitigations enabled. Each task provides the vulnerable source code, a short bug hint, and the corresponding binary; the agent must develop an exploit, achieve arbitrary code execution in a separate sandbox, and retrieve a secret string for automated verification. We report pass@3 over a random subset of runs, with no hard timeouts or output token limits.

blocks.text: On xdev-bench-hard, the checkpoint without these risk-reduction measures — no cyber-related data removal at mid-training and no cyber-related RL environment filtering — solves 90.5% of problems at pass@3; the final K3.1 Pro reaches 81.0%. The comparison shows that data removal meaningfully reduces cyber capability relative to what the same training pipeline would otherwise produce. At the same time, K3.1 Pro improves substantially over its predecessor, indicating that stronger general coding and long-horizon debugging capabilities generalize to cyber tasks even after targeted data removal. K3.1 Pro's cyber capability remains behind that of frontier proprietary models that have been publicly available for at least three months. We will keep evolving our internal benchmarks so that evaluation stays informative as model capabilities continue to advance.

blocks.text: Open-weight principles. These evaluations frame our open-weight release decision. First, we aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability. K3.1 Pro's offensive cyber capability is, by design, below what our pipeline can produce, and remains behind that of frontier proprietary models. Second, we intend to progressively raise the cyber capability available in open weights. We believe making K3.1 Pro available in a non-discriminatory way benefits people who need dual-use capabilities for defensive purposes. When a capable model is open and runs on infrastructure its users control, many more teams gain the means to audit the code they maintain — including legacy systems that rarely receive dedicated security reviews. We believe that letting this capability diffuse gradually — rather than concentrating it in a few proprietary systems — ultimately makes all software more secure.

inlines.text: BioMysteryBench dataset is drawn from the

Our Agents’ Last Exam dataset is drawn from the

, comprising 122 tasks, including 86 CLI tasks, with environment images aligned with the official Hugging Face release. We additionally assign a score of zero to runs that bypass the task’s stated requirements, such as retrieving answers online instead of performing the required analysis in Wireshark. OfficeQA Pro, OfficeQA Pro v2. GPT-6 Astra is evaluated with Codex, while all other models are evaluated with Claude Code. Each task provides the agent with the entire PDF corpus, with all PDFs rendered as images and no machine-readable text available. We observed instances in the trajectories of certain external models where they retrieved reference answers online; Consequently, we assigned a score of zero to these tasks.
Frontier Finance is evaluated with the official finance agent v2 harness.
HANDBOOK.md is evaluated using the official harness built on OpenHands, with evaluation tasks drawn from the benchmark’s early open-source v1 release.

Harvey Legal Agent is evaluated on a public dataset of 1,251 tasks using Artificial Analysis’s Stirrup harness, with performance reported as the all-pass rate (i.e., the percentage of tasks that pass all rubric criteria).
OSWorld V2.1 is evaluated with the Kimi Agent harness in the official OSWorld v2 repo, while GPT-6 Astra's score is taken from Muse Wonder's technical report.

DECK-Arena evaluates presentation generation on real-world queries, while Design Bench covers graphic design via direct and reference-image few-shot prompting; Both run models across python-pptx, pptxjs, and Kimi's in-house DSL in a harness with integrated search and image generation, using an automated grader calibrated on 10,000+ human judgments.
MCP Atlas. All models are evaluated on the 500-task public subset with a 100-turn limit, using Gemini 3.1 Pro as the judge.

BrowseComp. We adopt the context-compaction strategy used in the Claude model cards, triggered at 200K tokens. We allow a maximum of 500 steps; if this limit is reached before a task is completed, we force the agent to provide an answer, which is then judged. All BrowseComp runs are conducted with temperature=1.0 and top-p=1.0.
